title: Round Count and Statistical Distance Bounds
summary: Existing AES/SPN bounds can make statistical distance arbitrarily small by iteration, but their round-versus-distance tradeoff is loose; tighter quantitative bounds remain open.

formal_statement.body: Obtain tighter bounds relating the round count $r$ to statistical distance $\varepsilon$.

scope.domain: Quantitative security analysis of substitution-permutation networks using statistical distance.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine tighter quantitative bounds relating the round count to statistical distance.

progress.summary: The source explicitly calls a tighter tradeoff between the number of rounds and statistical distance an interesting open question. Existing AES/SPN bounds achieve arbitrarily small distance by iteration but have loose round dependence.
citation_labels: Tianren Liu et al., The $t$-wise Independence of Substitution-Permutation Networks
